text:
alex: onboarding request for tenant `acme-ml` in East US2. Need VNet + subnet layout, peering to shared-services hub, NAT gateway(s) for outbound, and a GPU quota bump (A100). Posting details and asking for help with quota/service limits.
maria: can you list exact IP plan and quotas you need? also are we using PrivateLink for storage/registry to avoid egress?
alex: yes on PrivateLink preference — want to avoid high NAT egress for large model downloads. here's the planned network footprint: 
```
vnet: redwood-acme-vnet (10.40.0.0/16)
subnets:
  - control-plane: 10.40.0.0/24
  - worker-gpu-az1: 10.40.1.0/23  # AZ1, up to ~510 IPs
  - worker-gpu-az2: 10.40.3.0/23  # AZ2
  - worker-gpu-az3: 10.40.5.0/23  # AZ3
  - infra (monitoring, bastion): 10.40.7.0/24
  - privatelink-endpoints: 10.40.8.0/26
  - peering-gateway: 10.40.9.0/28
```
We need peering from this VNet to `redwood-shared-hub` in the hub subscription. Peering should allow forwarded traffic to on-prem VPN. Route table: default route 0.0.0.0/0 -> NAT gateway.

Quota requests: 
- GPU quota (A100 class / NVMesh type): increase GPU instances from 8 -> 32 in East US2 (all AZs). This is for p4/a100 workloads, roughly want capacity for 16 active nodes initially.
- Public IPs: need two Standard Public IPs for NAT gateway (primary + warm standby) and +3 extra for load-balancer frontends in the infra subnet. Current subscription has 4 free, we need total 6.
- vCPU quota: increase Standard_NC/ND families (vCPU) by +256 in East US2 to support the above.
- Increase outbound SNAT port capacity: we expect many concurrent egress connections (model pulling + telemetry). Request ability to attach up to 8 public IPs to NAT gateway or alternative SNAT scaling.

devon: do we have a preference for NAT vs per-node SNAT? note Azure NAT Gateway has per-public-ip SNAT ports improvements, but cost for multiple public IPs/NATs adds up. PrivateEndpoint for blob/registry will save egress but not all traffic will go to storage.
maria: can we host model artifacts in the shared-registry behind PrivateLink? if so, we only need NAT for package repos and external API calls.
alex: yes, planning to put artifacts in shared storage + Private Endpoint to shared-registry (blob + ACR). Requesting security team signoff for PrivateLink access from this VNet.

infra-bot: Support case opened with Azure: SR#12345678901. Case linked to subscription 000-111-222. Requested GPU and public IP quota increases. Estimated response 3-5 business days.

quota-bot: SR#12345678901 update: initial review complete, asked for business justification and expected monthly spend. Please reply to the support case with estimated throughput and peak nodes.

alex: reply posted to SR with projected traffic: baseline 8 GPUs 24/7 + scale to 32 GPUs during load tests; monthly egress estimate ~50TB (models + telemetry). Also attached onboarding security checklist.

devon: quick notes on NAT sizing and cost tradeoffs:
- NAT Gateway standard SKU: ~$X/day per gateway + per-ip. For heavy pull workloads, prefer 2 public IPs initially; we can add more if SNAT hits limits.
- Alternative: use a small fleet of egress proxies (VM scale set) with standard public IPs behind a load balancer to control SNAT and caching. Cheaper for low-to-mid egress, but less resilient than NAT Gateway.
- Suggest we start with NAT Gateway + PrivateEndpoints for storage/ACR, monitor SNAT usage for 2 weeks, then reassess.

maria: note on routing: make sure peering has 'Use remote gateways' set appropriately for hub VPN. We'll need user-defined routes in peering-gateway subnet to force 0.0.0.0/0 -> NAT gateway in spoke.
alex: I'll attach a minimal ARM template for the NAT + subnet + peering to the onboarding ticket. sample snippet below: 
```json
{
  "type": "Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/subnets",
  "name": "worker-gpu-az1",
  "properties": {
    "addressPrefix": "10.40.1.0/23",
    "routeTable": {"id": "/subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.Network/routeTables/gpu-routes"}
  }
}
```

devon: pinging cloud-ops to ask for quota prioritization. If Azure needs a timeline, we should say we want production by 4/1.
alex: timeline noted (production target 2026-04-01). Also flagging cost owner: @maria to approve extra public IP/PATG costs.
maria: approved if we can keep egress < 100TB/mo, otherwise need finance sign-off.

alex: thanks all — I'll update the onboarding doc and post final SR link once quotas are approved.
